How a load runs — start to sealed

The whole chain, the way the newest build runs it — try every step live on the Loads and Money tabs with the fake RUGGS fleet:

🚪 Broker sends→ 🖥️ Desk accepts→ 🧑‍✈️ Driver assigned→ 🚛 Driver runs it→ 🔗 Receiver confirms on the link→ ⛓️ Delivery seals itself→ 🗄️ Lands in the Library — printable, emailable, downloadable

Fleet owners — your desk books it, your drivers run it, the record seals itself. One Desk and the boards are on the Loads tab; the Library — every record in one home — is on the Money tab.

What's new in this preview

Updated to the latest approved buildPREVIEW · SAMPLE ONLY

Now mirrors the newest approved builds — the simplified navigation (one Library for every record, one Desk with a role switcher, Loads on a single My Loads / Tracker / Boards switch, Money as one tab), the new Tax Worksheet in the Library, auto-add stops on planned routes — the planner's fuel, 30-minute break, and 10-hour rest picks land on the route as waypoints, announced on the route with one-tap Remove, with an opt-out switch in Settings → Driving (on by default) — and this: the Worth-It Advisor and True Rate now deduct your own factoring % and dispatcher % from a load's gross pay before judging it. The Advisor judges a load after your own factoring and dispatcher cuts are taken out, with the math shown line by line — fake RUGGS data only. Also new in this pass: the receiver signature pad (type the name or draw it — a drawn signature prints on the signed POD, and the sealed record notes how they signed), Money sectioned behind a sticky bar with the More directory folded into counted groups, one search box for your loads, drivers & paperwork, suggested next loads on the fleet board with their reasons printed leg by leg, and a paperwork door on every load — a broker drops the rate con, BOL, or POD straight into the load, no account. Also in this pass: pre-trip and post-trip inspections beside the HOS clocks on Drive — the pre-trip opens on its own at the first On Duty of the day — and a one-tap duty remark on every status change, stamped with city, state, and time on every log entry. Also in this pass: the regulatory audit fixes — the 70/8 or 60/7 cycle choice on the clocks card, split-sleeper done right, certified daily logs, the DOT packet with Email + PDF beside it, the 13-item inspection checklist with named repair certification, remarks that open the checklist, and a tightened qualification file. Nothing here is live or saved.

In the full app every price carries its source and age, and a price the app can't source shows as unavailable, never guessed. Fuel Coach (Diamond) adds speed & idle coaching from the same GPS data.

EX-TAX / IFTA-ADJUSTED PLAN — SAMPLE RUN: HOUSTON, TX → JACKSONVILLE, FL

The plan ranks stops by base price — pump price minus the state fuel tax — not by pump price. Two sample stops show why:

Stop A — Sample Stop, Mississippi · 214 mi ahead
Pump $3.44 − MS fuel tax $0.18 = base $3.26/gal · take 30 gal only
Cheapest pump on the route — but Mississippi's low fuel tax means most of that pump price is the fuel itself. Once the tax comes out, the base price is the worse deal, so the plan takes just enough here to reach Stop B.base $3.26/gal
Stop B — Sample Stop, Florida · 486 mi ahead
Pump $3.57 − FL fuel tax $0.429 = base $3.14/gal · take 85 gal — the big fill
The pump price looks higher, but Florida's higher fuel tax is most of the difference — and IFTA settles tax where the fuel is burned, not where it's bought, so that tax is not lost. What you really pay for the fuel is the base price, and here it's the best on the route.base $3.14/gal  BEST BASE
This plan — true cost
Pump spend $406.65 + IFTA settlement $2.73$409.38
Cheapest-pump plan — true cost
Pump spend $395.60 + IFTA settlement $23.90$419.50
Estimated saving — an estimate
Buying by base price instead of pump price, same route, same gallons$10.12

Sample prices are estimates and carry their source and age in the full app, like every price above; a stop with no price is never ranked or costed. Tank discipline is enforced on every plan: the tank never drops below reserve and a fill never goes past capacity.

A perfect day pays exactly 500 points, plus a +200 clean-week streak bonus. Points convert at $0.25 per 1,000 SM Points, paid in $STONER at the live price at payout, with a minimum conversion of 10,000 points (10,000 points = $2.50 worth of $STONER). Conversions open at launch — November 20, 2026 — for paying tiers, so until then this shows an honest “opens at launch” state. On Basic (free), sealed trips and on-time PODs earn half — 60 and 82 points — and there are no fuel-stop points, since fuel routes and the planner are paid-tier. Your points are yours — they never expire, and staying on the free tier never costs you your balance: free-tier points are never forfeited for staying free and never wiped by any season reset, and a free driver keeps and stacks his full balance, but he cannot convert while free — converting unlocks only when he upgrades to a paying tier; on upgrade the retained balance converts under the normal rules (10,000-point minimum). Full points panel on the Money tab.

CYCLE — YOUR CHOICE (REGULATORY FIX · SAMPLE)

The cycle is a choice, not a default: the driver picks it — or the fleet owner picks it for the whole fleet — to match the carrier's real schedule, so the clocks never overstate the hours a driver actually has.

Split-sleeper, done right: a sleeper period of 7+ hours paired with another break of 2+ hours — 10 hours total — counts as a proper split and extends the day the way the federal rule allows (sample line).

Inspections — truck + trailer, right beside the clocks. The first time you go On Duty in a duty day, the pre-trip opens by itself — once a day, skippable, never a hard block. Deliver a load and start a new one the same day inside the same 14-hour window, and the post-trip opens the same way. When a pre-trip seals, the flow offers Start driving — the order is On Duty → Pre-trip → Drive. And every inspection first reviews the last report's open defects — the federal pre-trip rule — so an open defect is in front of you before you roll, never buried.

The 30-minute break, the federal way: it's required after 8 hours of driving — not 8 hours on duty — and off duty, sleeper, or on-duty-not-driving time all satisfy it. Thirty minutes fueling counts.

Offline mode (sample)

No signal doesn't stop the record. Duty changes (HOS) and DVIR inspection saves made offline are captured on the device, in order, and seal automatically through the same seal paths when the connection returns — sealed at the captured time. An offline capture never poses as a sealed record.

Android Auto & Cab Mode (preview)

📺

Head-unit projection is not live yet — it arrives with the Play Store release. Try Cab Mode on the phone and the three template previews below. Nothing in this preview connects to a real vehicle.

What is Cab Mode? Cab Mode puts STONEMILES on the truck's own screen — the head unit — instead of a phone swinging on a mount. It is built for hotshots, commercial rigs and fleet trucks, and the new 2027 cabs & semis: a dually's factory dash running Android Auto, or the big factory screens landing in 2027 Peterbilt and Kenworth cabs and semis. Cab Mode fills that screen with what a load actually needs — your next turn big enough to read at a glance, your speed against the posted limit, ETA and miles left, your drive clock, truck stops, parking and weigh stations ahead, and road alerts that matter when you are hauling. No squinting, no reaching for the phone — eyes up, hands on the wheel, load moving. And nothing else in the cab does this: no other screen carries the load with it — the drive clock tied to your sealed trip, what to expect at the dock when you arrive, and a green route line at night. Basic includes the basic cab display; Gold, Diamond, and Fleet / Owner include the full version. No separate price — it is part of the tier.

Cab Mode is included by tier — it is never sold separately and has no price of its own. Basic gets the basic version: the glanceable Guidance screen. Gold, Diamond, and Fleet / Owner get the full version, which adds auto-open with guidance, voice directions on the cab display, the HOS tile, and the Stops ahead + Road alerts screens. Driver
Unit R-101 · Flatbed · FAKE DRIVERD. Carter
Commitment
Set by the driver himselfHome by Friday 6 PM

A commitment can be home by a date, home every N days, or home on weekends. This sample uses the first kind: home by Friday 6 PM.

⛔ Load #1062 would break it — bind STOPPEDBIND STOPPED · SAMPLE

Load #1062 — Birmingham, AL → Atlanta, GA (sample). The plain math: this load delivers Friday 4:10 PM. Add the 3 hr 20 min drive-home allowance and D. Carter gets home Friday 7:30 PM — 1 hr 30 min after his Friday 6 PM commitment. The check runs before the load binds, so the bind stops here. The load does not bind on its own.

No silent pass and no guessed arrival — delivery time plus the drive-home allowance is compared with the commitment, in plain words, before anything binds.

OVERRIDE — ONLY WITH A REASON, AND SEALED

The load above binds only if the right person explicitly overrides with a reason. The override — reason, commitment, and the math above — is sealed in the load record.

Who can override this one: D. Carter set this commitment for himself, so only D. Carter can override it — on the driver's phone. Dispatch cannot override it for him, and neither can the fleet owner from this Desk. A commitment the fleet set for a driver follows the fleet's own override rule.

Preview only: nothing overrides, binds, or saves here. In the full app the driver submits the reason, the override seals, and the load can then bind as overridden.

BOL & delivery — receive link, QR, three ways to sign (sample)

Bill of lading — Load #1042EN ROUTE · UNSIGNED
Mobile, AL → Dallas, TX · Pavers — palletized stone · 42,500 lbs · Shipper: Peacock Pavers Yard, AL · Receiver: Dallas receiver, dock 4
RECEIVE LINK + QR — ON EVERY BOL
stonemiles.app/receive/1042-DEMO

The QR prints right on the BOL and the link rides with it. The receiver opens it on their own phone — no app, no account — checks the freight, notes any damage or shortage, and confirms. That confirmation is the POD.

THREE DOORS AT THE DOCK — THE FIRST ONE USED SEALS IT

Docks sign three ways, and all three feed the same sealed record. Whichever door gets used first closes the delivery — the other two just show “already confirmed,” never a double entry.

Receive link: the receiver opens the link (or scans the QR), confirms the freight on their own phone, and signs with a fingertip. Fill the receiver side in below — in the full app this is the receiver's own screen.

Sign on the driver's phone: no link needed — the receiver signs right here on the driver's screen, name under it, any damage or shortage noted on the spot. That signature becomes the sealed POD.

Paper BOL: the driver prints the BOL (QR rides on it), the receiver signs the paper, and the driver photographs the signed BOL and uploads it as the POD. The paper is the signature; the photo seals it.

Evidence: sealed rate con + desk assignment · Confidence 99%

No external partner feed is connected — these updates post to the load's own tracking page only, and nothing claims otherwise. If an update can't be derived with confidence, it doesn't go out — it lands in the exception queue on the Desk instead (see the Desk at the top of this tab).

📄 Paperwork-to-pay — Load #1042 (sample)INVOICED · SAMPLE

The driver files a scanned BOL/POD, the app proposes the fields it read, and the driver confirms or corrects them. Once the delivery is sealed and the POD is confirmed, the paperwork finishes itself. The load and its tracking page show the same five-stage ladder:

Received
Confirmed
Sent
Invoiced
Paid

This sample load stands at Invoiced — Received, Confirmed, Sent, and Invoiced are reached; Paid hasn't happened yet.

Rate law: the tracking view shows the paperwork stage only — the rate prints on the invoice only, never on the tracking view.

Automatic reading isn't set up yet in this sample — the fields were checked by hand; nothing is guessed. In the full app, automatic reading needs a reading service connected; until then the app says so plainly and the driver checks the fields by hand.

READING THIS MONTH — THE RULES BEHIND THE CHIPS

Document expiry ladder: the sample DOT medical card expires Monday, Nov 30 — the red item on its day. The warnings ride ahead of it on the same 60 / 30 / 7-day ladder as the app's credential alerts: the 60-day warning fired Oct 1 (before this month opens), the 30-day warning sits on Sat, Oct 31 — “expires in 30 days — renew soon” — and the 7-day warning sits on Mon, Nov 23 — “expires in 7 days.” A card never lapses quietly.

Paydays stay “expected”: every Friday (Nov 6 · 13 · 20 · 27) is marked Payday — expected. A payday stays “expected” until the settlement is recorded paid — only then does it flip to paid.

Multi-day items run across their days: each committed load draws pickup → en route → delivery across its cells, the 34-hour reset spans Nov 14–15, and home time spans Nov 26–28 as one block — with the home-time deadline marker on Nov 25, the day before it starts.

PU = pickup day · DL = delivery day · EXP. = expected — a payday stays “expected” until the settlement is recorded paid. J. Rivera's row is the same week as the driver calendar above, seen from the desk.

DISPATCH MODE — HOW A POSTED LOAD LANDS (FLEET SETTING)

Assigned — a posted load lands on the driver's calendar as committed, no decline step.
Offered — the load shows as offered / pending until the driver accepts.

Offered is the default — the selection shown above. No fleet's world changes until its owner picks Assigned. Demo switch: flipping it here changes nothing and saves nothing.

↔ Reassignment — needs the driver's consent (sample) AWAITING CONSENT

Load #2110 — Memphis, TN → Little Rock, AR (sample) · Currently on M. Chen · Dispatch proposes moving it to S. Patel.

Reason, shown to both drivers: “Chen's approved home time starts Thursday — this delivery would run straight through it. Patel is empty in Memphis that morning.” (sample reason)

The move fires only when the current driver consents — until Chen answers, the load stays exactly where it is. You are holding Chen's phone for this sample:

The rule: a driver's refusal stands unless the FLEET OWNER overrides it with a stated reason — dispatch cannot override a refusal.

OWNER vs DISPATCH — SAME GRID, MORE LEVERS

The owner sees the same fleet grid as dispatch, plus the owner-only levers: overriding a refusal (with a stated reason the driver sees), the dispatch-mode setting above, and time-off approvals. Dispatch works the grid day to day; the owner owns the exceptions. And an owner-operator is the driver — same calendar, same loads and deadlines — wearing the owner hat only for his own approvals.

Preview sample only: fictional drivers, fictional loads — every button above is inert and answers with a demo note. Nothing consents, refuses, moves, or saves.

How the calendar helps — read it off the grid

🗓️Plan weeks ahead, not day by day. The whole week for 20 drivers sits on one screen — next week's gaps, resets, and home time are visible before this week's loads are even finished.
🏠Home time is protected before a load is ever assigned. The HOME blocks on the grid are commitments, not hopes — an assignment that would run through one gets stopped and explained, not booked.
⚠️Expiry warnings land on the calendar itself. CDL, medical, and TWIC warnings ride the 60 / 30 / 7-day ladder — you can see all three on this one week — so a credential never lapses quietly mid-run.
🚫No double-booking. One grid, everyone visible: two loads can never land on the same driver on the same day, because the desk would see it before it happened.
◐Offered is not assigned — and it doesn't look it. Offered loads sit dashed and amber until the driver accepts; assigned loads are solid. Nobody mistakes a maybe for a commitment.
👁️Each role sees the right grid. A company driver sees only his own calendar — never this fleet grid, never anyone else's week. Dispatch and the owner see all 20 rows.
👑The owner gets the same grid, plus the levers. Time-off approvals, the dispatch-mode setting, and overriding a refusal with a stated reason the driver sees — owner-only, on top of the grid dispatch works every day.

One day at Gulf Haul — the full app in motion

MONDAY, SAMPLE DAY · MORNING DISPATCH → ROLLING → DOCK → DELIVERY → PAPERWORK → PAY
🌅6:00 AM — Morning dispatch. The desk opens the grid above: 12 drivers under load, suggested next loads waiting with their reasons printed, one medical warning to chase, one time-off request to approve. The morning briefing and the notification badge already counted all of it.
🔎One search box. Dispatch types a town and gets the load, the driver, and the paperwork in one result list — no digging through five apps to answer one question.
🚛Rolling. Drivers run truck-legal GPS with route-ahead weather on the same screen as their hours — duty set with the status buttons, the DVIR done in the pre-trip flow, ELD synced. One truck crosses a dead zone and keeps capturing, its records marked “not sealed yet” until signal returns and they seal.
🅿️Parking that fits the clock. Tonight's stops are judged will / won't make it against each driver's remaining drive time — nobody is sent to a lot they cannot legally reach.
⏱️At the dock. Check-in starts the detention clock. The wait is timed, noted, and sealed as it happens — and the claim pack builds itself from that record instead of from memory at the end of the week.
🏁Delivery. The receiver signs the POD by link — typed or drawn — and the delivery seals itself. Status updates post to the load's public tracking page on their own; the one update that can't be derived with confidence doesn't go out — it lands in the exception queue for a human to decide.
🗂️Paperwork files itself. The broker's rate con and BOL came in through the load's paperwork door; on delivery the signed POD auto-sends, the invoice is generated, and the factoring pack is assembled — no re-typing, no chasing.
💰Pay lands. Settlements update, who-owes-me moves the delivered load off the list, drivers see exactly what they earned, and points land for the run. Every step of the day is in the sealed record — the whole company can prove its own day.

Sample walk-through — one invented Monday at a fictional company, shown to demonstrate the flow. Nothing above happened, and nothing in this preview runs it.

The full app in use — every surface, working

The showcase company touches every tab of the app every day. Here is the full spread — the same surfaces you can tap through on the other tabs of this preview, shown the way a 20-driver company actually uses them. All sample.

🏠 TODAY — the command center
  • Morning briefing per role — the desk's day and each driver's next move, counted and ready
  • Notifications that matter: credential warnings, offered loads, approvals waiting — badged, not buried
  • Global search — one box for loads, drivers, and paperwork
  • “What's my next move?” answered for every driver, all day
🧭 DRIVE — GPS & the road
  • Truck-legal GPS that knows the rig — height, weight, and HazMat shape the route
  • Route-ahead weather on the same screen as the drive
  • HOS clocks and duty status buttons — hours and loads, one screen
  • DVIR pre-trip inside the flow, not on a clipboard
  • Parking fit — every stop judged will / won't make it on the driver's clock
  • Fuel optimizer — stops picked by true cost, and fuel-card purchases checked against the truck's location; a mismatch gets flagged
  • ELD sync, plus offline capture — records held as “not sealed yet” until they can seal
  • Cab display and Android Auto glance screens for the desk's trucks on the road
📦 LOADS — the desk & the boards
  • One Desk with a role switcher — driver, dispatcher, owner, broker
  • Broker identity and payment-record checks before the first haul, not after a problem
  • DQF gate — dispatch is blocked while a driver's qualification file is out of order
  • Suggested next loads with the reasons printed, leg by leg
  • Detention clock and a sealed claim pack on every dock wait
  • Status updates post themselves to the load's public tracking page — the exception queue catches anything that can't be derived with confidence
  • POD signed by link, typed or drawn; the paperwork door on every load; paperwork auto-send and the invoice the moment a delivery seals
📅 CALENDAR — the week, protected
  • The 20-driver fleet grid above — plus every driver's own calendar underneath it
  • Home-time commitments enforced before assignment, not apologised for after
  • CDL / medical / TWIC expiry ladder — 60, 30, and 7 days out, on the calendar itself
  • Offered dashed, assigned solid — dispatch modes a fleet setting, not a habit
  • Reassignment by consent; a driver sees only his own calendar, the desk sees the fleet
💰 MONEY — pay, settled & sealed
  • Settlements and the true-net view — every driver sees exactly what a run paid them
  • Who-owes-me — accounts receivable worked in order, nothing ageing in a drawer
  • Invoices generated from the sealed delivery, and factoring packs assembled in one tap
  • Fuel-card mismatch check — a purchase that doesn't match where the truck was gets flagged for review
  • Profit & loss with QuickBooks / Xero sync — the books without re-typing
  • Points and rewards landing on every settled run
  • The Library — every load, signature, and settlement sealed, nobody edits history
⋯ MORE — truck, trailer & team
  • Dashcam coaching for the fleet — and an exoneration vault that can clear a driver after a wreck
  • Fault-code translator — dash codes in plain language, plus a maintenance log with countdowns
  • Predictive maintenance — flags raised across the fleet before a breakdown picks the place
  • Smart trailer and the reefer cold-chain log, riding with every load
  • Recruiting door — applications land straight in the Desk pipeline
  • Driver pulse check-ins and retention facts for the desk — home time kept and pay promises kept, counted where the owner can see them
  • Document vault, settings, languages, and cab mode — the rest of the toolbox

One workspace, every size of company

Delete the pile of apps. STONEMILES is one workspace with 50+ tools — and it scales by turning on the desk, not by bolting on another product. Same app, three sizes:

🚛 OWNER-OPERATOR — SOLO

One truck, no office staff — and it still runs like a company.

  • Truck GPS with loads and hours on one screen — the whole day in his pocket
  • Detention clock plus claim pack — dock time stops being free
  • Receiver signs the POD by link — typed or drawn, no paperwork chase
  • A paperwork door on every load — the broker drops documents straight in
  • Settlement and true-net view — what the run really earned, line by line
  • Who-owes-me and invoices — nobody's “the check is in the mail” survives a sealed record
  • Credential warnings 60, 30, and 7 days out — never an expired card mid-run
  • Maintenance log plus fault-code translator — the truck talks, he understands it
  • A fuel plan built on true cost, and points and rewards on every run
  • His own calendar approving itself — he is both sides of the desk, so his time off just commits
🏢 SMALL COMPANY — 2–10 TRUCKS

Everything the solo runs, plus a desk that keeps a small fleet honest.

  • Fleet board — every truck's status, location, and hours at a glance
  • Driver calendars with home-time commitments the desk cannot quietly break
  • DQF files audit-ready — dispatch blocked before an out-of-order driver ever rolls
  • Suggested next loads, matched per driver with the reasons printed
  • Global search across the whole company's loads, drivers, and paperwork
  • Pay book and settlements per driver — payday without the spreadsheet
  • Profit & loss with QuickBooks / Xero sync — books done without re-typing
🏭 LARGE COMPANY — THE 20-DRIVER SHOWCASE & UP

The full desk — Gulf Haul Freight above runs on exactly this.

  • Fleet calendar grid — every driver, every week, on one screen
  • Dispatch modes, Assigned or Offered, set once for the whole fleet
  • Reassignment by consent — refusals stand; only the owner overrides, with a reason the driver sees
  • Broker identity and payment-record checks before the fleet hauls
  • Factoring packs assembled in one tap, receivables worked in order
  • Dashcam coaching plus the exoneration vault across the fleet
  • Predictive maintenance, smart trailer, and reefer logs on every unit
  • Recruiting door feeding the Desk pipeline — the next 20 drivers arrive organised
  • Exception queue — the few things a human must decide, gathered in one place
  • Sealed records across the whole fleet — every load, hour, and signature, provable

That is the full app, in use, at three sizes of company — one workspace, 50+ tools, and the old pile of apps left behind. Everything on this page is SAMPLE / DEMO data for a fictional company; every button is inert and answers with a demo note. Keep tapping:

A person picks the winner — nothing auto-merges money records. The two versions sit side by side until someone chooses; the sync never decides a money record on its own.

Predictive maintenance — fault codes (sample)

🔧 Fault codes — in plain language
For the sample truck — 2021 Kenworth W900 · Unit 12
PREVIEW · SAMPLE ONLY

When the truck reports a fault code, the app translates the ones it knows into plain language with one of three urgency labels — stop now · service soon · watch — and drafts the work order itself. Sample codes only.

SPN 4364 · FMI 18 — reported Nov 14, 2026 (sample)SERVICE SOON
Plain language: the exhaust-cleaning (SCR) system isn't cleaning NOx as well as it should — check the DEF dosing and NOx sensors before it turns into a derate.
A work order was auto-drafted from this code — it's the top draft in the Maintenance log above, marked AUTO-DRAFTED FROM FAULT CODE, waiting for a human to confirm it.
SPN 520999 · FMI 31 — reported Nov 13, 2026 (sample)UNKNOWN CODE
Recorded exactly as reported: “SPN 520999 · FMI 31.”
The app doesn't know this code and never invents a meaning for it — no translation, no urgency guess. It sits in the record as-is for the shop to read off the truck.
⏳ Service-due flag — from the truck's own readingsESTIMATE
Computed from the truck's own readings — odometer and engine hours (sample): oil service estimated due in about 1,900 mi. It's labelled an estimate — an early heads-up, not a promise; the sealed Maintenance Countdown stays the record.

How sealing works

Every trip, load, and delivery gets a fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash) chained to the record before it. Change any old record and every fingerprint after it breaks — so a sealed sheet proves it wasn't quietly edited. On-chain anchoring stays off until a separate go-live call.

Verify & Audit — proof lookup (sample)

Verify & Audit proof lookup: every sealed record carries a QR and a short code. A broker, receiver, or auditor can look up the proof and check a record is genuine without an account — the code either matches the hash chain or it doesn't.

OpensNovember 20, 2026 — at launch

Points are earned only from GPS-verified events — for sealed work. They are not a token and are never sendable or tradable — conversion by the driver who earned them is the one exit, and conversion opens at the Nov 20 launch for paying tiers; for a free/Basic account it additionally unlocks only on upgrade to a paying tier. Until then no conversion can be made from this panel. Points keep earning in the meantime. This rate is a conversion rate, not a promise of earnings. On Basic (free), sealed trips and on-time PODs earn half points — 60 and 82 — and fuel-stop points aren't earned: fuel routes and the planner are paid-tier features. Your points are yours — they never expire, and staying on the free tier never costs you your balance: free-tier points are never forfeited for staying free and never wiped by any season reset, and a free driver keeps and stacks his full balance, but he cannot convert while free — converting unlocks only when he upgrades to a paying tier; on upgrade the retained balance converts under the normal rules (10,000-point minimum). If a paying account lapses for non-renewal and is later reactivated, conversion and cash-out stay held for 2 weeks from reactivation — sample: “Reactivated — your balance unlocks on November 9, 2026 while your account stays active” — and cancelling during the hold starts a fresh 2-week retainer.

Security Pack 2

🔐Account-takeover protection — authenticator 2FA for Owner & Dispatch, new-device sign-in alerts, an active-sessions screen, and sign-out-everywhere.
🚪Sign out, right up top — the Sign out button sits in the top bar beside the menu, and one confirm tap signs out this device. After signing out, only a real credential gets you back in — app PIN, Face ID / fingerprint, or the full sign-in under “Sign in with a different account.” There is no one-tap back-in.
📵Lost-phone kill switch — remote session kill and lock from any signed-in device; a fresh PIN is required before wallet, EIN, settlements, or exports open.
⛓Sealed access & export audit — who viewed or exported a driver's records is itself hash-chained; an owner viewing records seals an entry. One-tap cutoff ends a departed driver's access.
📍Location privacy rules — the company sees location on duty / on trip only. Raw GPS breadcrumbs auto-delete after 30 days; sealed trip records remain.
💵Money-movement step-ups — when conversion and cash-out activate: fresh verification for large amounts, velocity checks, and review holds, all shown plainly.

The Settings sheet (top right) mirrors the full app's Security Center with sample values. An independent penetration test is required before real money moves — stated plainly, not buried.

Driving

Voice alerts
Spoken warnings — overspeed, hazards, HOS, weather — hands-free
Banner alerts
On-screen alert banners while driving
Hill grade alerts
Steep-grade warnings with your live speed on the banner — downgrade and climb calls half a mile out, a gear-down / brake-check prompt at the crest, and the live grade readout beside your speed while you're on a grade. On the Drive screen and the Cab Mode Guidance + Road alerts screens.
Traffic lights
Signal markers on the Drive map and a “Traffic light ahead” pill on your route during guidance — locations only; the layer never shows a light's colour or state. This is the same switch as the Traffic lights chip in Layers & display above the Drive map.
Winter & weather alerts
Severe weather warnings matched to your route and ETA, plus the winter package: chain alerts (“Chains required ahead”) with the chain-up pullout noted, and snow depth calls like “4 to 6 inches expected across your next 90 miles.” On the Drive screen and the Cab Mode Guidance + Road alerts screens.
Enhanced map view
Satellite imagery + tilt on the Drive map. Turn this OFF to remove satellite and tilt entirely — the map returns to the plain road view.
Map style

Map style lives here in Settings → Driving — it no longer floats over the Drive map.

Map tilt
Tilt the Drive map view — set here, not on the map itself
Auto-pick best route
AI picks by safety → net pay → time, and logs its reason
Auto-add stops to my route SAMPLE
On by default. When you plan a route, the stop planner's picks are added as waypoints automatically: the best fuel stop by true cost when the tank needs a buy, a 30-minute break stop timed off your HOS break clock (folded into the fuel stop when they line up), and a 10-hour rest stop placed before your 11-hour / 14-hour clocks run out. The destination never changes, every added stop is announced on the route with one-tap Remove, and turning this off returns the planner to suggestions only — nothing auto-added.
Auto-start trips
Trip logging starts on its own once movement is detected
HazMat loads
When on, routing checks placard restrictions, tunnel bans, and permitted HazMat routes before offering a route

Privacy & data — Security Center

🔐 App PINON · SAMPLE
Stored as a salted PBKDF2-SHA-256 hash (120,000 rounds) — never as the PIN itself. 5 wrong tries locks the app for 15 minutes, and changing the PIN requires the current one.
🚪 Sign out & getting back inTOP BAR
Sign out sits in the top bar beside the menu; one confirm tap signs out this device. Getting back in always takes a real credential — app PIN, Face ID / fingerprint, or the full sign-in under “Sign in with a different account.” There is no one-tap back-in, and the signed-out screen shows no account name or email. Sign-out-everywhere and the active-sessions screen still live here in the Security Center.
🧾 EIN on fileENCRYPTED
AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest, and only ever shown masked: ••-••••1234. Reveal is owner-only, behind the PIN, and every reveal is logged and sealed into the audit chain.
💳 PaymentsIDEMPOTENT
Every charge carries a unique key, so a retried or double-tapped payment can never charge twice. Card numbers are never stored or touched by the app — they go only to the licensed payment processor at go-live, so there's no card data here to steal.
⛓ On-chain anchoring & escrowOFF
Off until a separate go-live approval. Records are sealed in the app's hash chain today; no keys live in the app and nothing moves on-chain in this build.
🧱 Wallet wallENFORCED
Company screens, logs, and every export carry zero wallet data — no setting changes that. The exports on the Money tab are built to prove it.
🔗 Hash chainINTACT
Chain head (sample): 8f2ce7a1… · PIN, payment, and security events seal into the same chain as trips and loads, and integrity is checked on open.
🌳 Daily Merkle rootANCHORING OFF
Each day's sealed records roll up into a single Merkle root (sample): 4d7a…c201. At go-live, that one root is what gets anchored on-chain — a single fingerprint proving the whole day, without exposing any single record. Anchoring stays OFF until the separate go-live approval.

About STONEMILES

STONEMILES by Stonervision

Built by a Trucker for Truckers. every mile, sealed.

Built by a Trucker for Truckers — one line for everybody who hauls: owner-operators running their own truck, company drivers, hotshots, and the fleet owners whose desks book the loads.

For fleet owners & dispatch: the Owner plan — company setup, driver codes, the dispatch chain (book it, assign it, watch it live), both broker doors, auto logs, the Library, and a wallet wall your drivers can trust.

For owner-operators: truck-legal routing, the state-line trip sheet with pay per state, detention proof, HOS clocks, and parking before your clock runs out.

For the blockchain generation: sealed hash-chained records and $STONER — staged honestly until launch, and not live in this preview.

This is a shareable interactive preview — Demo / Sample data only, not the live app. Subscriptions and wallet features activate at the app-store / token go-live. The full app is private to its driver — this preview carries no real accounts, trips, or records.
